## Knowledge

- oxlint runs type-aware with every rule as an error; oxfmt formats the code.
- A local plugin enforces boundaries: `apps/web` imports only `@kurasu/contract` and `@kurasu/slides` among the project's packages; `packages/core` imports no Cloudflare, Alchemy, Drizzle or jose; `packages/*` never import `apps/*`.
- TypeScript rules: `== null` instead of `=== null` or `=== undefined`; no enums (a const map and a derived type); named exports only.
- The tsconfig compiles with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`: an optional prop `?: T` rejects an explicit `undefined`. A prop every caller writes is required and typed `T | undefined`; a prop callers may omit is `?: T | undefined`.
- React rules: arrow-function components with a `Props` interface; React imported by name; conditional rendering with a ternary, never `&&`; no nested ternaries; one component per file; no destructured `useQuery` or `useMutation`.
- The project copies anti-slop into `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/` and adapts it as its own, with its generic and Effect rules.
- `@effect/tsgo` makes `tsc` fail on Effect diagnostics: missing services, `any` in error channels, global `Date`, `fetch` or `console` inside Effect.
- lefthook runs check on every commit; nobody commits with `--no-verify`. The tests run by hand with `pnpm test` before handing work over, because the API suite takes about a minute. turbo caches each package's tests until the package or one of its workspace dependencies changes.
- Tests are integration tests only, in `apps/api/test` (Alchemy's `alchemy/Test/Vitest` in dev mode, HTTP and WebSocket against the local stack) and `apps/web/test` (screens with the real router, the API answered by MSW, Testing Library on happy-dom). Tests live only there: the `test-location` lint rule rejects a test file anywhere else, and the root `projects` list names only the two apps. Before a package whose logic is too complex to cover through the API or the web gets its own tests, extend both the `test-location` rule and the root `projects` list to include it. Tests do not mock modules.
- Two web test helpers control when the mock server answers a request and what it answers. `heldResponse(method, path)` (`test/helpers/held-response.ts`) holds every request to the path until the test calls `release`, so the test can check the screen while the request is still waiting: a skeleton, a pending button. Released without a response, the requests fall through to the handlers already in place. `failingRoute(method, path, status = 500)` (`test/helpers/failing-route.ts`) answers the path with that status and a body no endpoint declares, as a failing server does.
- Pass the handlers that replace the page's own as the `overrides` argument of the test file's `openPage`, which calls `server.use` with them after the page's handlers and before the page renders. If the test calls `server.use` after the page opens, the requests that the page sends while it loads have already reached the page's handlers.
- On a machine under heavy load, some `/aula` tests can run past the 1 s that Testing Library's `findBy*` and `waitFor` wait by default. Run them again before changing them.
- Each API test file deploys its own stage: an empty D1 and R2, the migrations, and its fixtures loaded with `importFiles`. The tests in a file share that database, so each test uses its own records. The test stage sets `allowedDestinationAddresses` to the fixtures' emails; a link requested for an email outside the list makes the mail fail. A test reads the mail bodies from the files the local binding writes under `.alchemy/local/email`, and the sender, recipients and subject from the line the binding logs to the stage's Worker log under `.alchemy/log/<stage>/Api` (`test/helpers/sent-mail.ts`); see `alchemy/local-tests`.
- `app/vitest.config.ts` lists the two projects under Vitest 5's `projects` option; there is no `vitest.workspace.ts`. `happy-dom` and `msw` are also installed at the root, so the whole workspace resolves a single copy of vitest.
- The API project runs at most 4 test files at once (`maxWorkers: 4`): more stages starting together overload the local runtime and every file times out. Each run adds about 130 MB to `apps/api/.alchemy` (see `alchemy/local-tests`).
- The 101 MB upload test (A89) is skipped: under a full run the local runtime sometimes drops the connection mid-upload (EPIPE), and in production Cloudflare cuts a body past 100 MB before it reaches the Worker.
- There are no end-to-end tests. Rows marked `test + manual` in the test design are also run by hand with agent-browser against the local stack (`alchemy dev` and Vite).

Una acción al instante cambia la pantalla en cuanto el usuario actúa, antes de que responda el servidor. Cuando el servidor responde, la pantalla queda con los datos que devuelve el servidor. Una acción en espera deshabilita su botón y los demás botones de su diálogo, como Cancelar, hasta que el servidor responde. Su botón muestra un spinner. Mientras espera, el diálogo de confirmación no se cierra ni con Escape ni con un click afuera. Cuando el servidor responde, la pantalla muestra los datos que devuelve.

Qué forma toma cada acción depende de cómo la hace el usuario:

- **Al instante**: las acciones directas, un botón, un switch o un arrastre, sin confirmación ni formulario. Por ejemplo, deshabilitar una sesión que no es la destacada, dar acceso a un usuario, levantar la mano, marcar una pregunta como respondida, activar o cerrar una encuesta, reordenar las sesiones o mover la slide.
- **En espera**: las acciones que pasan por un modal de confirmación, un formulario o un diálogo. Por ejemplo, borrar material, una encuesta o una sesión, sacar el acceso a un usuario, crear una sesión o una encuesta, subir un archivo, hacer una pregunta, votar una word cloud, que pasa por su campo de texto, responder un feedback, que pasa por sus cinco emojis y su campo de texto, guardar el perfil o enviar un anuncio de novedades desde su modal.

Destacar una sesión, sacarle la marca a la destacada, deshabilitar la destacada y habilitar una sesión desde su modal quedan en espera, porque pasan por un diálogo que confirma qué se cierra: si fallan, el error aparece dentro del diálogo, que sigue abierto (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md)).

Cerrar sesión es directa pero queda en espera, porque no cambia nada que se pueda deshacer en pantalla: la web espera la respuesta y va al login. Votar una encuesta de opción múltiple o de escala también queda en espera, como la word cloud. La opción elegida muestra un spinner hasta que responde el servidor y las demás opciones se deshabilitan. Si el voto falla, la opción vuelve a como estaba y aparece un toast. Marcar un HTML como slides sigue la revisión de las slides (ver [API de las slides](api-de-las-slides.md)).

> [!NOTE] Por qué la forma depende de cómo se hace la acción
> La regla busca que ninguna acción deje al usuario sin respuesta: lo directo se ve enseguida, y lo que ya pasó por una confirmación o un formulario muestra que está esperando.

## Lo que el diseño deja para el programa

- Dónde se arma el batch y cómo devuelve las encuestas que cierra.
- Qué error responde cada rechazo nuevo.
- Dónde vive el control de la destacada para no repetirlo en cada escritura.
- Cómo la web cuenta los efectos para las confirmaciones.
- Qué acciones del profe pierden el parche optimista.
- En qué componentes entran el panel de preguntas, el modal y las confirmaciones.
- Cómo se reparte el cálculo del camino entre el inicio y el admin.

## Decisiones de esta etapa

- **NotFeatured**: un error nuevo, 409, para activar una encuesta o prender las preguntas destacadas fuera de la destacada. Las escrituras del estudiante no lo usan: conservan el 404 que ya devuelven para una sesión que no pueden tocar, así el estudiante no distingue una sesión vieja de una que no existe.
- **El batch en el store**: `SessionsStore.changeFeatured` arma el batch en `packages/database`, porque el core no ve drizzle y el batch toca cuatro tablas (wiki architecture). Es el primer store que escribe en tablas de otros stores; las otras opciones eran un servicio de base aparte o pasar sentencias del core, y las dos rompen el reparto de capas.
- **Avisos al aula**: la sesión que sale recibe `session`, `polls` y `hands`, porque el profe puede tener abierta su página en otra pestaña y las listas de su admin cambian.
- **El nodo del camino**: el inicio y el admin usan la misma regla, y por eso el cálculo vive en `rail-look.ts`.

Parte que se saltea: el callstack, porque es el modelo compartido que usan las demás ramas.

La columna `featured` lleva un índice único parcial con la forma de `codes_current_enrollment_unique` (`packages/database/src/schema.ts:28`). Ese índice deja a lo sumo una fila con `featured = 1` entre las no borradas. Una sesión borrada conserva su marca, pero el índice no la cuenta. Una sesión deshabilitada nunca la tiene, porque deshabilitarla la desmarca en el batch. `drizzle-kit generate` escribe `0004_featured_session` con dos `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT false NOT NULL` y el `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`. SQLite agrega una columna con default sin reconstruir la tabla, así que la migración no copia filas. Todas las sesiones existentes quedan con los dos campos en falso (design 1).

`changelog_entries.type` es `text` sin `CHECK` desde `0003_changelog_and_ids`, así que sumar `questions-opened` al enum de `schema.ts:170` no genera migración. Pasó lo mismo con el tipo `feedback` en la rama 1 del feedback.

### 2.1 Callstack · settled

```
 PATCH /api/admin/sessions/:id                                                [[app/apps/api/src/handlers/sessions.ts#AdminSessionsHandlers.update]]
-given { title?, summary?, enabled?, currentSlide?, currentStep? }
+given { title?, summary?, enabled?, currentSlide?, currentStep?, featured?, featuredQuestions? }
 │
 └─ Sessions.update(id, change)                                               [[app/packages/core/src/sessions/sessions.ts#Sessions.update]]
    ├─ existingSession(store, id) → SessionNotFound (404)                     previous
+   ├─ featured() → current                                                   la destacada de hoy, o ninguna
+   ├─ when change.featured is true and (change.enabled ?? previous.enabled) is false → SessionDisabled (409)
+   ├─ when change.featuredQuestions is true and not (featured after the change) → NotFeatured (409)
+   ├─ leaving = the session that stops being featured:
+   │    current, when change.featured is true and current is another session
+   │    previous, when previous.featured and (change.featured is false or change.enabled is false)
+   │    none, otherwise
+   ├─ when leaving is some
+   │  └─ store.changeFeatured(leaving.id, id, change)                         el batch, ver 2.3
+   │     → closedPollIds
+   │     ├─ changelog.drop({ questions-opened, leaving.id })
+   │     ├─ changelog.drop({ poll-opened, each closedPollId })
+   │     └─ classroom.notify(leaving.id, session · polls · hands)
+   ├─ otherwise
    │  └─ store.update(id, change) → SessionNotFound (404)                     [[app/packages/core/src/sessions/sessions.ts#Sessions.update]]
    ├─ classroom.notify(id, changedTopics(change))                            changedTopics suma featured y featuredQuestions a "session"
    ├─ when previous disabled and session enabled → changelog.record(session-enabled)
    ├─ when previous enabled and session disabled → changelog.drop(session-enabled)
+   ├─ when change.featuredQuestions is true and previous.featuredQuestions is false → changelog.record(questions-opened, name: session.title)
+   ├─ when change.featuredQuestions is false → changelog.drop(questions-opened, id)
    └─ session                                                                vuelve leída del store
```

Las cuatro acciones del profe llegan por este mismo pedido: destacar (`featured: true`), sacar la marca (`featured: false`), habilitar destacando (`enabled: true, featured: true`) y deshabilitar la destacada (`enabled: false`). Prender o apagar las preguntas destacadas (`featuredQuestions`) también entra por acá. Mover la slide y editar título o resumen siguen el camino de hoy, porque no tocan la marca. La regla es esta: cuando una sesión deja de ser la destacada, todo lo que pierde se escribe en un batch junto con el cambio pedido, y después la API saca las novedades y avisa al aula de esa sesión.

### 2.3 El batch · settled

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R["changeFeatured(leavingId, id, change)"] --> Q["select id from polls where session_id = leavingId and status = 'active' and deleted_at is null"]
    Q --> B
    subgraph B["batch de D1, en orden"]
      direction TB
      B1["update sessions set featured = 0, featured_questions = 0 where id = leavingId"]
      B2["update polls set status = 'closed' where id in (activas)"]
      B3["delete from raised_hands where session_id = leavingId"]
      B4["update sessions set (change) where id = id"]
      B1 --> B2 --> B3 --> B4
    end
    B --> S["get(id): la sesión ya cambiada"]
    S --> O(("{ session, closedPollIds }"))

    classDef read fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#2563eb,color:#1f2937
    classDef write fill:#ffedd5,stroke:#ea580c,color:#1f2937
    classDef ok fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#16a34a,color:#1f2937
    class Q,S read
    class B1,B2,B3,B4 write
    class O ok
```

La primera sentencia desmarca la sesión que sale antes de que la última marque la nueva, así el índice único nunca ve dos destacadas (acceso-a-datos.md). Cuando `leavingId` es la misma sesión del pedido, que es el caso de sacar la marca o deshabilitar la destacada, la última sentencia aplica `featured: false` o `enabled: false` a una fila ya desmarcada y no cambia nada más. B2 cierra solo las encuestas que leyó la consulta previa, por id. Si entre la consulta y el batch el profe activó otra encuesta, esa encuesta queda activa, y la nota lo acepta: el profe solo activa encuestas en la destacada, y la destacada es la que está cambiando en este mismo pedido. Si una sentencia falla, D1 no aplica ninguna y el pedido responde 500.

`sessions.update` también sale del batch cuando `change` tiene un campo que no es una columna. La sentencia B4 se arma con el `statements.update` del repositorio (`packages/database/src/repository.ts:228`), que ya admite batch.

-│  ├─ visibleSession(sessions, poll.sessionId) → PollNotFound (404)          [[app/packages/core/src/sessions/visible-session.ts#visibleSession]]
+│  ├─ featuredSession(sessions, poll.sessionId) → PollNotFound (404)        ← la sesión es la destacada
 │  ├─ …
-│  └─ changelog.drop({ poll-opened, poll.id })
+│  └─ (sin drop: la primera respuesta ya no saca la novedad)

-│  └─ visibleSession(sessions, sessionId) → SessionNotFound (404)
+│  └─ featuredSession(sessions, sessionId) → SessionNotFound (404)

-│  └─ visibleSession(sessions, question.sessionId) → QuestionNotFound (404)
+│  └─ featuredSession(sessions, question.sessionId) → QuestionNotFound (404)
 └─ Hands.raise · Hands.lowerOwn                                              [[app/packages/core/src/hands/hands.ts#Hands.raise]]
-   └─ visibleSession(sessions, sessionId) → SessionNotFound (404)
+   └─ featuredSession(sessions, sessionId) → SessionNotFound (404)

    ├─ findPoll(id) → PollNotFound (404)
    ├─ when content change and not draft → PollNotDraft (409)
    ├─ when transition not allowed → InvalidTransition (409)
+   ├─ when change.status is active and the poll's session is not featured → NotFeatured (409)
    └─ …
```

`findOpenQuestion` es el único lugar donde pasan votar y borrar una pregunta, así que el cambio llega a las dos escrituras desde ahí. Las lecturas del estudiante siguen con `visibleSession`: el inicio lee las preguntas, las encuestas cerradas y el material de cualquier sesión habilitada. `classroomOf` ya exige la destacada (`sessions.ts:100`) y la toma de `featured()`, que ahora lee la marca. La regla es esta: toda escritura del estudiante sobre una sesión exige que sea la destacada, y si no lo es responde el mismo 404 que da hoy para una sesión que no ve. Activar una encuesta exige la destacada, y si no lo es responde `NotFeatured`.

Cuando el switch está prendido y hay otra destacada, muestra el aviso con `FeaturedEffects`. "Habilitar" manda `enabled: true` y, con el switch prendido, `featured: true`, en un solo pedido.

**FeaturedEffects** dibuja la lista de lo que se pierde. Cuenta las encuestas activas y las manos de la sesión que sale. Agrega "Se apaga el modo de preguntas destacadas." cuando esa sesión tiene `featuredQuestions`, y termina con "Las preguntas sin responder y la slide quedan como están.".

**ConfirmDialog** suma un slot `content`, debajo del texto, y `confirmIcon`, porque hoy el botón de confirmar siempre lleva el tacho. `ConfirmAction` pasa los dos tal como llegan.

## 8 Standards · settled

- wiki `architecture`:
  - `featured`, `featuredQuestions` y `NotFeatured` se declaran con Schema en el contract.
  - El batch vive en `packages/database`, porque el core no ve drizzle.
  - D1 no tiene transacciones, así que el cambio de destacada va en un solo batch.
- wiki `api`:
  - La marca viaja como campo de `SessionSummary`, sin endpoint propio.
  - Las cuatro acciones son el `PATCH` de la sesión.
  - Las preguntas de la card usan `GET /questions?sessionId=`.
- wiki `web`:
  - El panel entra por un slot de `HighlightedSession`.
  - Las confirmaciones son `ConfirmAction`, con un slot nuevo en `ConfirmDialog`.
  - Cada hook se arma sobre `useApiQuery` o `useApiMutation`.
  - Las acciones al instante llevan parche optimista; las que esperan, error dentro del diálogo.
  - Va un componente por archivo, en `features/<topic>/`.
- wiki `fence`:
  - `== null`.
  - Sin enums: `railLook` devuelve un literal.
  - `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` para los slots opcionales.
  - Render condicional con ternarios y sin anidar.
  - Los tests van en `apps/api/test` y `apps/web/test`.
- `app/docs/architecture/invariantes.md`:
  - Toda escritura del estudiante exige la destacada.
  - El backend controla aunque la web ya lo haga.
- `app/docs/architecture/carga-y-acciones-de-la-web.md`:
  - Las cuatro acciones con diálogo quedan en espera.
  - Deshabilitar una no destacada y el switch de preguntas destacadas son al instante.
- `app/docs/architecture/acceso-a-datos.md`:
  - El batch desmarca antes de marcar.
- `app/AGENTS.md`:
  - Lo que este program design cambie de las notas se registra en `app/docs/architecture/`.
- `AGENTS.md` global:
  - Bloques separados.
  - Sin variables intermedias innecesarias.
  - Comentarios solo para el porqué.
  - Commits convencionales.

content.text:
The whole program design is on the canvas at **http://localhost:5190**. It's written to `program-design/kurasu.md` and based on `feat/feedback-de-sesion` at `c4cf12a`, without the uncommitted changes. Two questions are still open; the other decisions come from the design, the notes, the prototypes or the code at `c4cf12a`, and each one names its source.

**The 8 branches:**
1. **Database model:** `featured` and `featured_questions` on the session, with a partial unique index and migration `0004`. `questions-opened` is a new changelog type and doesn't need a migration.
2. **`PATCH /admin/sessions/:id`:** a single request handles featuring a session, removing the mark, enabling it as featured, disabling the featured one, and the featured-questions switch. When a session stops being featured, everything it loses is written in one D1 batch together with the requested change. After the batch, the API removes the matching announcement items and notifies that session's classroom.
3. **The rule:** a new `featuredSession` check sits next to `visibleSession`, and every student write goes through it. Activating a poll is also blocked outside the featured session. The first poll response no longer clears the "Encuesta abierta" item.
4. **Student home:**
   - The featured card gets a slot that holds a new `FeaturedQuestions` panel. The panel reuses the existing question components.
   - `EarlierSessions` becomes `OtherSessions`.
   - A shared `railLook` function decides each timeline node for both the home and the admin.
5. **Session admin page:** a new `FeaturedSwitch`, a new `EnableSessionDialog`, and the 3 confirmations built on `ConfirmAction`. `ConfirmDialog` gets a slot for the list of what the session loses, which `FeaturedEffects` builds. Changes that wait for the server no longer update the screen before the response.
6. **Session list:** a `FeaturedLabel` with a star, and the same timeline rule as the home.
7. **Teacher's classroom panel:** a new `FeaturedQuestionsSwitch`, and no Activar button outside the featured session.
8. **Standards.**

**Open questions** (cards on the canvas, in branches 3 and 2):
- **Q1, what a rejection for "not the featured session" returns.** My proposal: a new `NotFeatured` (409) for the teacher's actions, and the student's writes keep returning today's 404. The alternative is `NotFeatured` for both sides, which adds it to 5 endpoints.
- **Q2, where the batch lives.** My proposal: `SessionsStore.changeFeatured` in `packages/database`, which would be the first store that writes to other stores' tables. The alternative is a separate port in core with its own adapter, so each store keeps writing only to its own table.

I fixed one inconsistency in a screen mockup: a disabled session showed a pending "Preguntas abiertas" item, but disabling turns featured questions off. That state now shows the list empty.

## Lo que el diseño deja para el programa

- Dónde se arma el batch y cómo devuelve las encuestas que cierra.
- Qué error responde cada rechazo nuevo.
- Dónde vive el control de la destacada para no repetirlo en cada escritura.
- Cómo la web cuenta los efectos para las confirmaciones.
- Qué acciones del profe pierden el parche optimista.
- En qué componentes entran el panel de preguntas, el modal y las confirmaciones.
- Cómo se reparte el cálculo del camino entre el inicio y el admin.

## Decisiones de esta etapa

- **Q1 · NotFeatured**: un error nuevo, 409, para activar una encuesta o prender las preguntas destacadas fuera de la destacada. Las escrituras del estudiante no lo usan: conservan el 404 que ya devuelven para una sesión que no pueden tocar, así el estudiante no distingue una sesión vieja de una que no existe. La web no deja hacer ninguna de estas acciones fuera de la destacada, así que el rechazo solo llega con una pantalla vieja (el usuario aceptó la propuesta).
- **Q2 · El servicio arma el batch (C2)**: `Sessions.update` coordina el cambio de destacada. Pide a `SessionsStore`, `PollsStore` y `HandsStore` sus escrituras sin ejecutarlas, con `writes`, y las corre juntas con el puerto `Batch`. `writes` es la versión diferida de los métodos de escritura de `Repository`, y `repositoryOf` la arma desde las `statements` que ya tiene, así que todos los stores la heredan sin código propio. Se descartó `SessionsStore.changeFeatured`, que seguía el patrón de `MaterialsStore` (un store que escribe en tablas de otros), y un método `Write` por caso en cada store.
- **Avisos al aula**: la sesión que sale recibe `session`, `polls` y `hands`, porque el profe puede tener abierta su página en otra pestaña y las listas de su admin cambian.
- **El nodo del camino**: el inicio y el admin usan la misma regla, y por eso el cálculo vive en `rail-look.ts`.

content.text:
I applied your three voice messages to the record (`program-design/kurasu.md`) and the canvas, and exported it again. Q1, Q2 and Q3 are settled.

- **Q1:** I took the proposal as you approved it. The student's writes keep today's 404 and the teacher's get the new `NotFeatured` (409).
- **Q2, option C2:** `Sessions.update` coordinates the batch.
  - `Repository` gets `writes`, a version of the existing write methods that returns an opaque `Write` instead of running it. `repositoryOf` builds it from the `statements` it already has, so every store inherits it.
  - A new `Batch.run(writes)` port in core runs the writes together; `D1Batch` implements it in `packages/database`.
  - I redrew the request flow and the batch diagram for this.
- **Q3, the student home:**
  - The list below is titled "Todas las sesiones" and includes the featured session, with or without one; "Otras sesiones" and "Sesiones" are gone.
  - The featured session's node shows a star instead of its number.
  - The components follow the "featured" name: `FeaturedSession`, `AllSessions`, `AdminFeatured`, and `SessionLinks` takes `featured`.
- **Admin list:**
  - The featured session has the star on its node and no "Destacada" chip.
  - No node shows a number; disabled sessions get an empty dashed node.
  - "Sesión N de M" is gone, from the list's top card and from the Contenido card. The dialogs now name the other featured session by its title instead of "la sesión 3".
- **Finding the featured session once:** `ContentTab` gets it with a new `useFeaturedSession`, a `select` over the admin's session list, and passes it to both switches. The page's own session already says whether it is the featured one; the list is only needed to know which other session is. The `select` function is defined at module level so it doesn't recompute on every render.

**Conflicts with the source:** these decisions contradict:
- `design.md`;
- `estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md` and `novedades-por-mail.md`, which still say "Otras sesiones", the chip and the numbers;
- the 3 prototypes.

I listed them under "Cambios a la fuente" in the record. Following the program-design skill, they get recorded in the docs at the end, in one pass.

Nothing is open on the canvas now. If you don't have more corrections, I'll mark the root settled and then record the source changes in the docs and prototypes, which needs your approval of the draft.

---
name: "write-documentation"
description: "Write or update a note in the project's docs folder explaining how one part of the system works, following the project's own charter and templates. Use when the user wants something documented, a mechanism written up, a note brought back in line with the code, or when mahou:design hands over a settled tree to record."
argument-hint: "<what to document, or the design tree to record>"
---
Load mahou:basics first, then mahou:docs. Then read `.mahou/write-documentation.md` if present.

# Write documentation

A note explains how a part works, in the present tense, and it is what someone reads instead of the code when they need to understand that part. This skill writes one, or brings one back in line with the code.

Resolve the docs folder as `docs` says, and read the charter and the target folder's README before writing a line. The charter decides the headings, the callouts, the diagrams, the wrapping, the frontmatter, the naming rule and how the indexes work. Where it is more specific than anything here, it wins. This skill carries no template body.

Most of the time a draft already exists. When mahou:design hands over a tree, each settled branch carries mechanism-first prose and a validated diagram, and writing the note is mostly moving that text into place. When the user asks for a mechanism to be written up, the code is the source and a `mahou:code-scout` reads it so the reading stays out of this conversation.

## 1. Pick the folder, and say which

Use the charter's folder table and, when the project's `CLAUDE.md` has a section on where each kind of change is documented, that section. Announce the folder and the reason in one line before writing. A note in the wrong folder is worse than a missing one, because readers find it, trust it and never look for a second copy.

Search the folder first and **prefer extending the note that already covers it**. A new section in the right note beats a new note beside it, and near-duplicates are how an index stops being readable. Check the name against every file in the docs folder before creating one; the charter usually says why a collision matters.

## 2. Write it

The charter owns the shape. The content rules are the framework's:

**Overview, then mechanism.** The overview says what the part is and is responsible for, in a few sentences a reader can stop after. Then the shape of the data, what calls what, in what order, in the sections from the template's menu that the subject needs and in the order that reads best, as `docs` describes. This is the bulk of it. A reader should be able to follow the part without opening the source.

**Explain the code, do not reprint it.** A declaration belongs in the file it lives in, where it is typechecked and stays current. What a reader cannot get from that file is why each part exists and who asks it, so the surface goes in a table of what each member answers, and the behaviour goes in prose or a diagram. A snippet survives only where the code *is* the insight, at two to four lines.

**The reasoning goes beside the thing it justifies, never as the note's structure.** Opening with the argument makes the reader meet the case for the design before the design. Keep the argument, since it is what lets a decision be revisited rather than re-argued, in the callout form the charter names, next to the mechanism. State the actual reason, not its provenance: "a strict test would freeze a thing already overlapping a wall", not "because the investigation showed".

**Every section explains something that exists.** A section that only introduces, summarizes or lists what other sections hold does not belong.

**A diagram whenever the subject has a shape.** A state machine, a data model, a sequence or a request's path all read faster drawn. Follow the charter's convention; where it names mermaid, do not draw in ASCII, and validate every diagram with superpowers:mermaid before the draft is shown. Place each diagram next to the prose it illustrates.

**An attachment sits where the prose refers to it.** A prototype, an image or an exported drawing goes where the charter puts attachments, linked at the point the prose needs it, with a caption that names what it shows. The note keeps no local or scratch path to the file.

**Strip the working session out of the note.** The tree or code a note comes from may name projects, tools, repositories and the current implementation; the note gets shared, so the draft drops them. In the draft:

- Name roles, not products, when the design is generic: "the assistant" rather than a product's name, unless the design is that product's alone.
- Name another note or tool only when the design depends on it, and then as a link at the point of dependency, never collected in a list at the end.
- No component, library or package names.
- No description of the current implementation or of what a repository still lacks; those descriptions belong to tasks.
- No sentences about who owns a piece of work.
- Never describe the prototype's controls or its file.
- Cut any sentence that compares the design with how things work today.

## 3. Describe the present

No "used to", no "previously", no "no longer", no "replaced by". A rejected alternative is *considered and not chosen, because…*, a standing reason, not a history of the argument.

This matters most when updating, which is most of the time. Change only what actually changed; if a section still describes the code correctly, leave it exactly as it is. Insert new behaviour without disturbing what is there. Delete behaviour that is gone; do not annotate it as removed. A note rewritten wholesale to accommodate one paragraph is a diff nobody can check.

## 4. Check the draft before anyone sees it

Run superpowers:unslop over the draft. It governs the prose; where it disagrees with the charter or the template about form, the charter wins. The known case is emoji heading prefixes, which unslop removes and the seeded template requires; the same holds for callout syntax and for bold on domain terms the charter asks for. Then dispatch a `mahou:documentation-reviewer` with the draft, the charter, the folder README and the template, and apply what it reports: those are departures from rules the project wrote for itself, so applying them is not a decision. Anything it reports that turns on the content rather than the form goes to the user as a question.

Then show the whole draft in the conversation and wait. Nothing lands in a file the user has not seen.

**How a draft is shown.** Plain markdown in the reply, never quoted, never as a code block, never in the browser. One paragraph of prose first: what changes and why. Then, per note, a bold line with the note's path, and for each edit one line of prose naming where it lands ("Replace the last sentence of <section>:", "New section before <section>:", "Append to <section>:", "<table>, <row>, <column>:"), with the section names as they read in the note, followed by the edit itself exactly as it will read in the file, headings and mermaid blocks included. A horizontal rule separates notes. A new note is shown whole under its path line with no location lines. The location lines are the only prose between edits; everything else after the opening paragraph is draft.

## 5. Land it in its index

Write the agreed draft. **Link it from at least one existing note**, or nobody reads it.

Then check how the folder's index works. A generated index means the note appears by existing, *provided its tag is right*: confirm the tag against the charter and the neighbouring notes, because a wrong tag drops a note out of its index silently, with no error anywhere. A hand-maintained table means adding this note's row and nothing else; do not touch the others.

## 6. Say what you wrote

Which note, which folder, which sections are new or changed, and what you deliberately left untouched. If reasoning went into a callout, quote it: it is the part written on the user's behalf, and it is short enough to read.

## 🏠 Inicio del estudiante

En el inicio, el estudiante ve solo las sesiones habilitadas, en el orden de la lista del profe. Arriba está la sesión destacada, la que tiene la marca. Es la única desde la que se entra al aula. Debajo, "Otras sesiones" lista todas las demás habilitadas en el orden del profe, también las que vienen después de la destacada. Al costado de esa lista, un camino une un círculo por sesión: las sesiones anteriores a la destacada llevan el check de terminada, y las que vienen después no llevan check ni número. Cada card muestra el resumen, las encuestas activas, donde el estudiante vota o deja su feedback, y los links a Material, Encuestas y Preguntas, sin cantidades. Cada link abre un modal, que en celular es una hoja desde abajo y en escritorio va centrado. Cada card que se pliega muestra un caret, que apunta hacia abajo cuando está plegada y hacia arriba cuando está desplegada, como la lista de Presentes. Una sesión de "Otras sesiones" muestra su material, sus encuestas cerradas y sus preguntas para leer, y en ella no se pregunta ni se vota.

Con las preguntas destacadas abiertas, la card destacada muestra el panel de preguntas arriba de las encuestas activas: el campo para preguntar, las tres preguntas más votadas y las del estudiante, en orden de votos. "Mostrar N preguntas más", debajo de la última, despliega la lista completa dentro de la card, y "Mostrar menos" la vuelve a plegar. Sin preguntas, el panel muestra el campo y "Todavía no hay preguntas. Hacé la primera.". Las respondidas no aparecen. El estudiante pregunta, vota y borra las suyas con confirmación, con los mismos pedidos que usa el aula, y después de cada acción la web vuelve a pedir la lista. La card también tiene el link Preguntas, que abre el modal con la lista completa.

Sin destacada, el inicio no muestra la card de arriba: muestra solo la lista, titulada "Sesiones", con todas las habilitadas y sin check ni número en el camino, y nadie entra a ningún aula.

Con `?sesion=<id>` en la URL, el inicio despliega la card de esa sesión entre las otras sesiones y hace scroll hasta dejarla en el centro de la pantalla. Es el link que lleva el mail de un anuncio (ver [novedades por mail](novedades-por-mail.md)). Si el id es el de la destacada, el de una sesión deshabilitada o borrada, o no existe, el inicio se ve como sin el parámetro. El parámetro queda en la URL, así que al recargar la card vuelve a desplegarse.

La lista de sesiones trae, en cada una, si es la destacada y si tiene las preguntas destacadas abiertas, y la web toma la destacada de esa marca. La web pide las encuestas activas de la destacada y, si tiene las preguntas destacadas abiertas, sus preguntas.

El inicio no recibe avisos: una encuesta que el profe activa o cierra, un cambio de destacada y las preguntas de los demás aparecen en el inicio cuando la web vuelve a pedir sus datos, cada cinco minutos, o cuando el estudiante vuelve a cargar la página (ver [componentes](componentes.md)).

[Prototipo del inicio del estudiante, en celular y escritorio](../prototipos/inicio-responsive.html)

## 🛠️ Admin de las sesiones

El profe ve la lista de sesiones, crea una nueva al final de la lista, las reordena arrastrándolas, y llega desde ahí a Usuarios (ver [login y acceso](login-y-acceso.md)). El número de una sesión es su posición en la lista. La destacada lleva el chip "Destacada".

[Prototipo de la lista de sesiones del profe](../prototipos/admin-sesiones.html)

La página de una sesión tiene las pestañas Contenido, Encuestas y Aula. En esa página, el profe habilita o deshabilita la sesión con el switch de su card, y una deshabilitada se borra desde la misma card. Debajo del switch de habilitar está el switch "Destacada", que se prende solo con la sesión habilitada. En Contenido edita el título y el resumen. ## 🧭 Orden y páginas

Una lista termina siempre ordenada por id, después de los órdenes que se le piden, así que el orden es total. Quien lista indica, para cada orden, si los vacíos van primero o último. Si no lo indica, van primero en orden ascendente y último en descendente. Por ejemplo, la lista de usuarios del profe va por nombre, con los que todavía no completaron el perfil al final, y después por email.

Una página tiene como mucho 100 filas. La siguiente se pide con la última fila de la anterior, y el repositorio arma la condición que trae las filas posteriores a esa, con cada campo del orden, vacíos incluidos.

> [!NOTE] Por qué el tope de 100 vale solo para listar
> El tope evita que un endpoint que lista filas devuelva una cantidad sin límite, como la lista de usuarios. La lista de novedades usa un tope menor, de 50. Las queries propias que juntan datos, como los conteos de las encuestas o las manos de una sesión, traen todo lo que corresponde en una sola query y no llevan tope.

## ✍️ Escrituras y batches

Crear y actualizar escriben y después vuelven a leer la fila, para devolverla decodificada. Borrar sin la opción de devolver lo borrado lee la fila y después la borra, en dos idas. Con la opción, la base borra y devuelve las filas en la misma sentencia. Insertar o actualizar es siempre una sola sentencia, así que dos pedidos a la vez sobre la misma fila no se pisan.

Cada escritura existe también como sentencia sin ejecutar. Varias sentencias, de una tabla o de varias, corren juntas y en orden en un batch de D1. Si una falla, D1 no aplica ninguna. Por ejemplo, regenerar el código de registro marca el código vigente como borrado y crea el nuevo en un batch, así que nunca queda la app sin código vigente.

> [!NOTE] Por qué una sentencia de batch no devuelve filas
> D1 devuelve las filas de un batch tal como están en la tabla, con los nombres de las columnas y las fechas como números, sin pasar por el mapeo que hace el query builder. Para no devolver filas con una forma distinta de la que declara su tipo, una sentencia de batch no devuelve nada. Quien necesita la fila la lee después del batch.

> [!NOTE] Por qué hay type guards en el repositorio
> Sobre una tabla genérica, el query builder no puede tipar las filas que devuelve una escritura. Tampoco puede tipar el cambio de un borrado lógico ni el de un insertar o actualizar. El repositorio les da su tipo con type guards en lugar de aserciones. Los type guards comprueban la forma de lo que llega antes de usarlo: que sea una lista de filas y que las claves del cambio sean columnas de la tabla.

## 🧩 Queries propias

Un store escribe su propia query cuando el repositorio no puede expresarla o la resolvería con más idas a la base. El repositorio lee una sola tabla por vez y corre una operación por sentencia, así que las lecturas que unen tablas o cuentan, y las escrituras que tienen que caer juntas, quedan en su store:

| Store | Query propia |
| Preguntas abiertas | el título de la sesión | `Se abrieron las preguntas de la sesión "<título>".` |

El asunto no lleva el número de la sesión, que el estudiante no ve. El cuerpo lleva, en este orden, el mensaje del profe tal como lo escribió, las novedades incluidas y el link a la sesión. Sin mensaje, el cuerpo empieza por las novedades. Sin novedades, lleva el mensaje y el link. Las novedades no llevan link propio: el único link del mail es el de la sesión. Si la sesión es la destacada en el momento del envío, el link lleva a la home, donde la destacada está arriba. Si no, lleva a la home con `?sesion=<id>`, y la home abre esa sesión entre las otras sesiones y la deja en el centro de la pantalla (ver [estados de encuestas y sesiones](estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md)). El mail no saluda

> [!WARNING] El link de un mail viejo a la destacada
> La API decide si la sesión es la destacada en el momento del envío. Después de un cambio de destacada, un mail viejo con el link a la home lleva a una home con otra destacada arriba, o sin destacada, y la sesión del anuncio queda plegada entre las otras sesiones. Al revés, si una sesión anunciada con `?sesion=<id>` pasa a ser la destacada, el link lleva a la home y no abre nada más, porque la destacada ya está arriba.

No lances subagentes: hacé todo vos.

## Qué hacer

Copiá estos tres prototipos de `app/docs/prototipos/` a `.scratch/preguntas-en-la-card/docs-draft-pd/prototipos/`, editá solo las copias y no toques `app/docs/`:

- `inicio-responsive.html`
- `admin-sesiones.html`
- `admin-sesion.html`

Las rutas son relativas a `/home/agus/workspace/filadd/agentic-engineering-famaf-extension-course/`. En cada archivo, cambiá solo lo que dice abajo. Los estados, los controles y el resto quedan como están.

## Cambios

### `inicio-responsive.html` (inicio del estudiante)

1. La lista de abajo se titula "Todas las sesiones" siempre, haya destacada o no. Desaparecen los títulos "Otras sesiones" y "Sesiones". La lista ya incluye a la destacada, así que el contenido de la lista no cambia.
2. El nodo de la destacada en el camino (el nodo `live`, hoy rojo con el número) lleva una estrella en vez del número, sobre el mismo rojo. Ningún nodo lleva número.
   - La estrella tiene que llenar casi todo el círculo: unos 26 px en el nodo de 44 px, y unos 20 px en el de 32 px del celular. El check es de 20 px, así que la estrella queda más grande.
   - Usá la estrella rellena que ya define `admin-sesiones.html` (`star-fill`, un path SVG). Copiala al mapa de íconos del inicio si no está.
3. Si un link `?sesion=<id>` apunta a la destacada, el prototipo despliega su card en la lista como con cualquier otra sesión. Si el prototipo trata ese caso, ajustalo; si no lo trata, no agregues nada.
4. Actualizá la descripción del prototipo (el párrafo de ayuda arriba) donde mencione "Otras sesiones", "Sesiones" o el número de la destacada.

### `admin-sesiones.html` (lista de sesiones del profe)

1. Sacá el chip "Destacada" (`featChip`) de la card de arriba y de la card de la lista.
2. Ningún nodo del camino lleva número:
   - la destacada (`live`) lleva la estrella sobre el rojo, con el mismo tamaño que en el inicio;
   - una deshabilitada (`lock`) lleva el nodo punteado vacío, sin número;
   - el resto queda igual: check antes de la destacada y vacío después.
3. La card de arriba (hero) pierde la línea "Sesión N de M", el chip y la etiqueta "Habilitada". Queda el título, el resumen y Abrir.
4. Actualizá la descripción del prototipo donde mencione el chip o los números.

### `admin-sesion.html` (admin de una sesión)

1. La card de Contenido pierde el kicker "Sesión 2 de 6". Revisá también el encabezado o los títulos de pantalla que repitan "Sesión 2 de 6" (por ejemplo, la línea 207, `text: 'Sesión 2 de 6'`), y sacá ese texto donde aparezca a la vista.
2. Los diálogos nombran a la otra destacada por su título, no por "la sesión 3":
   - el aviso del modal Habilitar dice `Hoy la destacada es "Tooling y skills" y deja de serlo:`;
   - la confirmación de destacar dice `"Tooling y skills" deja de ser la destacada:`.
3. Actualizá la descripción del prototipo si menciona el número.

## Cómo verificarlo

Abrí cada copia con `agent-browser` y recorré los estados que tocaste:

- inicio: un estado con destacada, uno sin destacada y la vista de celular;
- lista: "Destacada la 2, habilitadas hasta la 4" y "Habilitadas, ninguna destacada";
- admin de una sesión: Contenido, el modal Habilitar con otra destacada y la confirmación de destacar.

Mirá cada screenshot y corregí lo que no coincida con los cambios de arriba. Revisá también la consola por errores de JS. Al terminar, cerrá la pestaña de agent-browser.

## Informe

Respondé con:

- una línea por archivo con lo que cambiaste;
- lo que no pudiste hacer;
- las rutas de los screenshots.

name: "unslop"
description: "Cut AI tells from prose meant to be read as a document. # Unslop

Edit text to remove AI patterns.

## Process

1. Run a first round: one opus agent, every rule below, the documents in the pass.
2. Verify each finding, then rewrite. Preserve meaning, match intended tone.
3. Run a second round: a fresh agent, the rewritten documents, and the first round's applied report. It checks every applied fix is still in place and flags anything that changed back; verify and re-apply what really slipped, and the pass ends.

## How to scan

The pass is two rounds: the first finds, the second guards what the first fixed.

A fresh agent each round is the point. An agent that has seen its own last report defends the report, repeats what you rejected, and stops looking for what it missed. The second round's agent sees the first round's report on purpose. Its job is not to re-litigate the findings but to verify they survived.

The author cannot run this pass alone, whatever the rules say. Whoever wrote a sentence already decided it earns its place, and that is the judgement the rules ask for.

Agents write nothing. When the text is a draft not yet on disk, save it to a temporary file first so it does not travel through the dispatch message. When the pass covers several documents, one agent takes all of them in the same round, since a sentence that repeats what another document already says is only visible with both open.

### Prompts

The first round:

```
You are doing an editing pass. Read <the file or files>. Do not edit anything.
Do not read anything else.

Apply ONLY the rules below. Read every sentence, and at each one ask what the
reader does differently because of it. Flag the sentence when the answer is
nothing, when it is the answer an earlier sentence already gave, or when it
breaks one of the rules. Report only what one of these rules covers.

RULES:
<every rule under Patterns to detect and fix, verbatim, numbers included>

EXCLUSIONS: an adjectival participle ("the bullets that are missing", "before a
change is done") is not a passive under 29, and an adverb that changes
the truth of the sentence ("skip it silently", "usually already") stays.

<file>:<line> | rule <n> | "<exact quoted span>" | <proposed rewrite>
Only sentences with a finding get a line. End with a line TOTAL: <n>.
Nothing else. No preamble, no summary.
```

You are verifying an editing pass. Read <the file or files> and the report
below. Do not edit anything. Do not read anything else.

For every finding in the report, check the rewritten text still carries its
fix: the pattern the finding cited is gone and the rewrite kept every fact.
Report only findings whose fix is gone or undone, in this format:
<file>:<line> | rule <n> | "<exact quoted span>"

Ningún círculo lleva número. Cada card muestra el resumen, las encuestas activas, donde el estudiante vota o deja su feedback, y los links a Material, Encuestas y Preguntas, sin cantidades. Cada link abre un modal, que en celular es una hoja desde abajo y en escritorio va centrado. **app/docs/architecture/estados-de-encuestas-y-sesiones.md**

🏠 Inicio del estudiante, first paragraph. Replace from "Debajo, "Otras sesiones"…" through "…ni check ni número.":

Al costado de esa lista, un camino une un círculo por sesión: las sesiones anteriores a la destacada llevan el check de terminada, la destacada una estrella sobre rojo, y las que vienen después no llevan nada. Desplegada en la lista, la destacada muestra también "Entrar al aula", y su modal de preguntas deja preguntar y votar. Cualquier otra sesión de la lista muestra su material, sus encuestas cerradas y sus preguntas para leer, y en ella no se pregunta ni se vota.

# Test design with canvas

`test-design` and the skills it loads keep their procedure: roots, branches, classifications, partitions, matrices, facts, dropped rows, recording and ending.

When the user asks for a fast track, or fast track is already on in the session, load mahou:fast-track after mahou:canvas and before starting, unless it is already in context. It changes some of this skill's engagement rules.

The document is `canvas/test-design.tldr.json` in the change's scratch folder. The record stays `test-design/<repo>.md`; write a tree's change into it whenever the canvas changes, and draw the canvas from it.

## Roots on a map of the system

The candidate roots go on the canvas as a map of the system, under a title naming the change and the order the trees are worked in.

- **Each tree is an `area`**, labelled with its letter, its repository or deployable, and what it is to the rest of the system, such as `B <service>/: what a client calls`. Lay the areas out in the order work flows through them, whoever starts it on the left; put the tree that every other one imports along the bottom.
- **Each candidate root is a blue card** inside its tree's area. Its first line is an empty checkbox, `☐`, for the user to tick, then the root's id and its entry point; its second line is `e.g. <scenario>`, one or two scenarios through that entry point, an error case among them.
- **A candidate that is not a root is a grey dashed card** with the reason, such as a piece that runs only inside another entry point, or a migration, checked by one manual row.
- **Arrows join the cards that hand work to each other**, each labelled with the action one card asks of the other, such as `create` or `start`.

Tell the user to tick or cross out cards with sticky notes or by voice.

## Each branch is a classification tree

Each branch is an `area` labelled `<id> <root> · <status>`, inside its tree's area. Branches stack down their tree's area, and the trees sit side by side.

Draw every branch of a tree at once, each one whole: its root, classifications, partitions and matrix, labelled `proposed`. This replaces `test-design`'s one level and one branch at a time. A branch, and everything on it, stays `proposed` until the user approves it. Open the next tree once the user has approved every branch of the one before.

Draw each branch with `canvas`'s `classificationTree`, which lays out the root, the classifications, the partitions and the matrix. Keep each branch's spec as data in a script in the canvas folder. When a branch changes, such as a row turned manual or a partition added, call the helper again with the same name.

- **The root is a blue box** at the top, with the entry point and what it is given.
- **Each classification is a violet box** under the root, joined to it by a line with no arrowheads.
- **Each partition is a green box** under its classification, joined the same way, with a short label.
- **The matrix goes under the tree.** On the left, a narrow `★` column sits before `row · what the test does`, separated from it by a vertical dotted grey line; on the right, the header reads `expected · kind · setup`. Header labels are grey. Each row is one line: `★` in the first column when `isNew: true` and blank when the test already exists in the suite, its id and summary next to it, a filled dot under the centre of each partition it picks, and its expected outcome, kind and setup on the right. Dotted grey lines run between the rows and down each partition's column.
- **A row run by hand is orange**, its `★`, its text and its dots, whether it is `test + manual` or `manual`. Its expected outcome adds what the check observes by hand.
- **Dropped rows and deleted tests get grey lines under the matrix**, `Dropped: <reason>` and `Deleted: <test and reason>`. When either list is empty, nothing is drawn for it.
- **A branch with one row** draws its root and that row, with no classifications.

## Questions

A question goes inside the branch it is about, beside the classification, partition or row it discusses. A question about a root goes beside its card on the map. The branch's Agent note goes under the questions.

- **A question is a card with a violet border and no fill**, titled `❓ Q<n> · <title>`, then the body, which gives the situation and ends with the question. The card has no fill so it differs from the filled violet classification boxes.
- **Follow-ups stay inside the base question's card**, one at a time, until the question closes. The card holds, top to bottom: the base question, a summary box, one Agent note, and the current follow-up as a card of its own.
- **The summary box**, a solid grey rectangle labelled `Summary · Q<n> so far`, holds what the question has settled. Rewrite it each round; never add a line per answer.
- **When the question closes**, delete the card, redraw the branch with what it settled, and update the record.

## Messages from the agent

Everything you would say in the chat goes on the canvas, as an Agent note: a grey dashed rectangle labelled `Agent`, in the branch, tree or question it is about. One note at the top of the canvas says how to read the drawing and lists the implementation tasks the trees surfaced. Keep one Agent note per place and replace its text each round.

Follow the wiki indexes to the testing entries for the runners the repositories use, and read each repository's own testing conventions where the project keeps them, usually its `CLAUDE.md`: they decide the test level and the naming rule the rows follow.

# Test design

This skill applies the Classification Tree Method. Decompose a test object into the aspects that influence its behaviour, the classifications. Split each classification into disjoint classes, the partitions. A test case is a combination that picks one class per classification. Every question at every level is about what varies, how it is partitioned, and which combinations matter.

Takes a design the user has settled and produces, per repository, a tree whose leaves are the test cases and manual validations that prove the change, plus the combination matrix each branch resolves into. The matrix is built before any code exists so that whoever implements the change receives it as input. When the design tree is not at hand, the notes that record the design carry the decisions.

## How the tree is built

The user and the skill build each tree together, level by level: roots, then for one branch at a time its classifications, its partitions and its matrix. Every candidate comes from something already decided: a design leaf, a note's section, a fact read from the code. The skill shows the candidate for confirmation. The user confirms, cuts, merges or adds, and the next level opens on that answer.

The tree uses `design-tree`'s marks: `pending`, `open`, `settled`. Show the whole tree when the roots are confirmed, when a branch settles and at the end; otherwise show only the branch being worked. Row ids carry a letter per tree in the order the trees are worked and a running number across that tree: `A1`, `A2`, `B1`. A row can then be named from anywhere later.

## Roots

One tree per repository the change touches, worked from the repository the others depend on outward: the one that owns the data first, then the ones that consume it, then the one a person uses. When the order is not evident from the design, ask.

- On a service, a root is an entry point whose behaviour the change touches: an endpoint, a job, an event handler, a command, any way into the code. List the candidates from the design and, when code exists, from the diff, with what the change does in each, and let the user drop the ones the change does not reach. An entry point the change only crosses without altering its outcome is not a root; say why when the user asks.
  - A data migration has no root and no classification of its own. The other rows assume it ran. One manual row, outside the classifications, checks that its upgrade and its downgrade work.
  - A piece that runs only inside another entry point, such as a processor that executes during a read, is a classification of that entry point's branch, not a root.
- On a user-facing surface, a root is a main flow the change touches, including returning to a screen the user already completed when the change stores something there. The tree for such a surface covers each state a screen can show and each action that moves between them, so it is more exhaustive than a service's.
- On a user-facing surface, each placement of a flow, such as the same dialog opened from two parts of a page, is its own root. Each placement gets rows for every state and action the other placements cover.
- On a service, when two roots reach the same code the change adds, read the code to find which root reaches the added code on the usual path, and let the user confirm. The usual root carries the full matrix. The other root's branch covers only what that root's path adds, such as the states the root starts from. The branch title states that scope. Under that branch, list each classification the usual root already covers, with the rows that cover the classification, so none is hidden.

## Working a branch

Open one branch at a time, each on the approval of the previous.

1. **Classifications.** Read the existing test suite for the root's entry point, then derive the classifications from the inputs, states and outcomes the change affects: the input the entry point receives, the state it starts from, the configuration it reads, the responses of the systems it calls, the actor and how the actor arrives, and the outcome itself when the outcome branches. A classification that only the existing suite exercises, and that the change leaves untouched, stays out of the branch. Two sources add classifications to that list:
   - **Shared code the change alters.** List the code the change alters that other cases of the entry point also run through, such as a query, a helper or a component that every poll type passes through. The branch adds the classification that separates those cases, and the existing tests that run through the shared code become rows of the matrix as regression rows.
   - **Variants settled earlier.** Each variant that the design, the notes, the prototypes or the conversation named in an earlier stage is its own partition, so every decision gets a test.

   Show each classification with the design leaf, the shared code or the variant it comes from. Rules the user applies and the skill proposes when it sees them:
   - Two classifications whose partitions determine each other are one classification. If every partition of the first fixes the partition of the second, merge them and carry the expectation on the partition.
   - A classification with one interesting partition scopes the branch instead of staying a classification when no existing test in the root's suite exercises the other partitions. State the scope in the branch title.
2. **Partitions.** One list per classification, each partition with its expected effect when the design fixes it. Two partitions that the code treats identically are one partition, unless one of them is a variant settled in an earlier stage. When every input takes the code down the same path, the root is one row. A partition the design does not decide is asked, not filled in.
3. **Matrix.** One row per case inside the branch's classifications, including the cases the existing test suite already covers and the cases the change adds. Never drop a row because an existing test already covers it. A row picks one partition per classification. Every partition appears in at least one row, and the pairs of partitions that interact appear together. Columns: a narrow `★` column (`★` when the row is a new test added by the change, blank when the test already exists in the suite, whether kept as is or updated to match the row), the row id, a one-sentence summary of what the test does (not the test's function name), one column per classification, the expected outcome, the kind (`test` for an automated test through the entry point at the level the repository's conventions name, `manual` for a validation by hand against the running system, or both), and the setup column. Some rows need environment preparation: a seeded record, a configuration, a variant of an input. The setup column names that preparation and never includes test names. The skill builds the matrix and proposes the manual picks; the user adjusts rows and settles the picks.

Pick the manual checks from the test rows: a picked row's kind becomes `test + manual`, and its expected outcome adds what the check observes by hand. On a service they always include the most common flows and the most common error cases. A row is `manual` alone only when no automated test can check it. Schema rejections are not manual picks. On a surface whose repository has no test runner, every row is manual; whether it has one is a fact read from the repository, surfaced when the tree for it opens.

## Facts

The design is settled, so read the code whenever a partition, an expectation or a root depends on how the code behaves, without waiting to be asked. Before stating the state a root's rows start from, trace the entry point's call order up to the code the change adds: what runs before it and what is created after it. A starting state taken from the design alone is a guess. Surface every fact read this way in the level it affects; never apply one silently. When a fact contradicts a decision already settled, say so in the first sentence. A row whose expectation the code cannot meet is either corrected or becomes an implementation task; the user decides which, and record the task under the branch so the implementation receives it.

## Dropping rows and deleting existing tests

A row is dropped, never silently, when no realistic input reaches it. Examples of the kind of reason, not a list: two systems sharing the same schema cannot produce a validation error between them; a malformed response from another of our services is a programming error, unless the design makes one side validate the response's shape; input that the request type cannot carry, such as a field the request does not declare, never reaches the code; a value that only a hidden record carries cannot appear in a response; a state the flow cannot re-enter cannot be observed. State the reason in one line under the branch (`Dropped: <reason>`), so the row is not proposed again.

When the change alters or removes behaviour so an existing test in the suite no longer applies and is not updated as a row in the matrix, list it in one line under the branch (`Deleted: <test and reason>`). When no existing test is deleted, omit the line.

## Recording the design back

Questioning a tree settles more than tests: a member the design missed, a mechanism renamed mid-round, a gap the partitions exposed. Collect every amendment the trees produced, from what was read during the work; when the set is incomplete, say so. The user settles each one: amend the note, or carry it as an open decision.

Then run mahou:write-documentation once, handing it every settled amendment together, so it weighs how the changes affect the whole documentation rather than only the pieces the trees touched. An amendment landed during test-design follows the recording discipline the design itself followed: the text is shown before it lands, and unsloped with the note it joins.

## Ending

When every tree is settled, show them together with, per tree, the row range, the count of test rows and the manual picks, and list the implementation tasks the trees surfaced. Write each settled tree with its matrix to the change's scratch folder, at `test-design/<repo>.md`, so the trees survive the session. mahou:implement takes the trees as input; mahou:validate runs the manual rows.

Then check the scratch folder as mahou:basics says under Status.

## What this skill is not

It does not write tests and does not run anything. It does not propose a case the design does not imply.

# Diseño de tests · kurasu (`app/`) · feedback de una sesión

Repositorio: el del curso, carpeta `app/`. Fuente: `../program-design/kurasu.md`, `../design.md` y `app/docs/architecture/feedback-de-sesion.md`. Canvas: `../canvas/test-design.tldr.json`.

Orden: A API → B web. En el mapa, la web (`B`) a la izquierda llama a la API (`A`). Las pruebas a mano en local son filas marcadas `test + manual`.

Cada rama tiene las clasificaciones que el cambio afecta: las del feedback y el tipo donde el feedback cambia código compartido. Las filas sin ★ son tests que ya existen y cubren ese código contra regresiones. Los tests que ya existen y siguen igual quedan nombrados bajo cada rama, en "Sin cambios en la suite". La columna `★` marca las filas nuevas; vacía, un test que ya existe y se actualiza.

## Enmiendas al design

- Q4 · Un texto en blanco no se acepta. La web no manda `text` cuando el campo queda vacío o tiene solo espacios y saltos de línea, y la API responde `400` si `text` llega así. Un texto con contenido se guarda tal cual, con sus espacios. Cambia el design (rama 1, "sin texto, la clave no está"; rama 3, "el texto puede ir vacío"), la nota `feedback-de-sesion.md` ("si llega vacío o no llega, la respuesta se guarda con el punto solo") y el program design (rama 2: `Polls.vote` ya no saca el texto vacío; `ResponseValue.text` lleva un check de que no esté en blanco, compartido por la web y la API).
- Q1 · En el panel del aula, un borrador de feedback se ve como lo ve el alumno: los cinco emojis con sus extremos y el campo de texto, sin poder tocarlos. Cambia el program design (rama 5: `PollPreview` suma la rama de feedback y entra en la lista de archivos) y la nota `feedback-de-sesion.md`, que dice que el panel muestra la tarjeta con las barras pero no cómo se ve un borrador.

import json

def status(branch):
    return "open" if any(q["branch"] == branch["key"] for q in QUESTIONS) else "settled"


def span(branch):
    ids = [r["id"] for r in branch["rows"]]
    return f"{ids[0]}–{ids[-1]}" if len(ids) > 1 else ids[0]


# ---------------- record
def ascii_tree(branch):
    lines = [branch["root"]]
    cls = branch["classifications"]
    for i, c in enumerate(cls):
        last = i == len(cls) - 1
        lines.append(("└─ " if last else "├─ ") + c["name"])
        for j, (_, label) in enumerate(c["partitions"]):
            lines.append(("   " if last else "│  ") + ("└─ " if j == len(c["partitions"]) - 1 else "├─ ") + label)
    return "\n".join(lines)


def table(branch):
    cls = branch["classifications"]
    head = ["★", "Fila", "Qué hace el test", *[c["name"] for c in cls], "Esperado", "Kind", "Setup"]
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(head) + " |", "|" + "---|" * len(head)]
    for r in branch["rows"]:
        picks = []
        for c, key in zip(cls, r["picks"]):
            picks.append("–" if key is None else dict(c["partitions"])[key])
        cells = ["★" if r["isNew"] else "", r["id"], r["summary"], *picks, r["expected"], r["kind"], r["setup"] or "–"]
        out.append("| " + " | ".join(cells) + " |")
    return "\n".join(out)

      "Orden: A API → B web. En el mapa, la web (`B`) a la izquierda llama a la API (`A`). Las pruebas a mano en local son filas marcadas `test + manual`.", "",
      "Cada rama tiene las clasificaciones que el cambio afecta: las del feedback y el tipo donde el feedback cambia código compartido. La columna `★` marca las filas nuevas; vacía, un test que ya existe y se actualiza.", "",
      "## Árbol", "", "```", "Diseño de tests · feedback de una sesión"]

md += ["```", "", "## No son raíces", "",

# Tasks

Takes a design the user has settled and produces the tasks that implement it, in the project's tracker, whatever it is.

## The tracker

Read `.mahou/implement.md`. The project names its task tracker there, the tool that reaches it, and the states a task moves through. When that file is absent, ask the user which tracker holds the backlog and how to reach it, for example an MCP server, a CLI, or a file path. Whatever the mechanism, the skill works through it and never invents a second source of truth.

When the user says the project has no tracker, say so and write no tasks; mahou:implement works without one.

## Deriving the tasks

The tasks come from what was settled, never from imagination. Read the design notes, the program design files in the change's scratch folder, and the test design notes. Derive the candidates:

- One task per actionable outcome, not per built thing: split a deployable along the parts the architecture names, keep a migration whole, split an integration along its client, its steps, and its rules.
- One task per piece the design names as risky enough to verify on its own, such as a proof or a spike that stays.
- The test matrices do not become tasks; they are listed in the briefs the tasks generate.

Show the candidates grouped per repository, each with what it requires in one or two sentences and the notes that ground it. The user settles each one: create it, reshape an existing task into it, or drop it.

## Writing through

Create and update through the tracker's mechanism, one call per task, in the order the work will run. Close a dropped task with a short comment naming why. Never delete one silently. Touch nothing else in the tracker.

## Ending

Report the tracker's state for this change: what was created, reshaped, dropped, and left standing. mahou:implement picks the list up from here.

## What this skill is not

It does not design, does not decide a task's shape without the user, and does not move tasks through their working states; that belongs to the agents that implement them.
